rows.feature: Cmd+V right after the toolbar's New slide button
rows.interaction: Copy a rectangle, click New slide in the toolbar, press Cmd+V
rows.evidence: Run 3, three tries: a new slide each time (title-1, title-3, title-4), Cmd+V put nothing on it (objects 0 -> 0), no notice. Follow-up 4 (deck untitled-20260916-i56x) case (a): the keyboard focus after the button click is button[toolbar.newSlide], the active slide is the new one, Cmd+V pastes nothing and the slide stays a title slide; case (b): a click on the empty new slide first, then Cmd+V: the copy lands at 200,150 (the source position) and the slide becomes a canvas; case (c): Edit > Paste right after New slide works the same way (200,150). Follow-up 5 (deck untitled-20260916-zv03) on a slide that is already a canvas: with the focus on the filmstrip card just clicked, Cmd+V pastes nothing; two Escapes leave the focus on the card and Cmd+V still pastes nothing; a click on the empty sheet, or the slide's own rectangle selected, or Tab to a handle, and Cmd+V pastes at 200,150. Mechanism: the stage handles the paste only when it owns the keyboard focus; the toolbar button and the filmstrip card keep it after a click.
rows.why: Carrying a card to the next slide is the seller's most common paste; the key must land where the seller expects.

rows.feature: Cmd+V with the keyboard focus in the filmstrip

rows.evidence: Follow-up 5 (deck untitled-20260916-zv03): after the filmstrip card click the focus is div.ts-card.is-current[filmstrip.slide.title-1]; Cmd+V pastes nothing (objects 4 -> 4, no notice, no console entry); two Escapes leave the focus on the card and Cmd+V still pastes nothing; a click on the empty sheet (focus div.ts-stagewrap.ts-sheet) then Cmd+V pastes shape-2 at 200,150.

rows.feature: Paste keeps the source position on another slide

rows.interaction: Select a rectangle, press Cmd+D

rows.feature: Edit > Duplicate and Edit > Delete (the menu)
rows.interaction: Select a rectangle, Edit > Duplicate, then Edit > Delete
rows.evidence: Follow-up 8, two runs (decks untitled-20260916-nj1q and 31fi): A clicked (chip "Shape", focus on the sheet); Edit > Duplicate (row enabled) 5 -> 6 objects, chip "Shape"; Edit > Delete (row enabled) 6 -> 5, chip none; the slide count stayed 1. The object removed was the original A, not the copy: after the two menu actions A's block was gone from the stage and only the copy remained (the third run lists the shapes left). Edit > Duplicate leaves the original selected, where Cmd+D selects the copy (run 3 row 33 and follow-up 5 case 6), so a Delete straight after the menu duplicate leaves the seller with the copy 16 px right and down of where the object was. Run 3 row 41 read 5 -> 5 three times while the stage held another slide; the Edit rows then acted on the current slide, which is what they do with no object selected (follow-up 5 case 8).
rows.why: The menu route.

rows.feature: Cmd+D with nothing selected on the canvas
rows.interaction: Click the empty slide (or leave the focus on the page body), press Cmd+D

rows.evidence: Follow-up 5 case 7 (focus body): Cmd+D took the deck from 2 to 3 slides and made the new slide current; Cmd+Z 3 -> 2; Cmd+Y 2 -> 3. Case 8 (focus body after a menu): slides 1 -> 2.

rows.interaction: Cmd+D on a rectangle, Cmd+Z, then Cmd+Shift+Z, Cmd+Y, the toolbar Redo or Edit > Redo
rows.why: Undo then redo is the seller's way to compare before and after; an empty redo loses the duplicate.
rows.evidence: Follow-up 5 case 7, route 1 (deck untitled-20260916-zv03): A clicked (chip "Shape", focus on the sheet) -> Cmd+D 5 objects -> Cmd+Z 4 -> Cmd+Shift+Z 4 (nothing redone) and the toolbar Redo button reads aria-disabled true. Run 3 rows 42 to 44 on the first slide: Cmd+D 5 -> 6 -> toolbar Undo 5 -> toolbar Redo 5; Cmd+D 6 -> Edit > Undo 5 -> Edit > Redo 5 (both rows enabled); Cmd+D 6 -> Cmd+Z 5 -> Cmd+Y 5. Four drives, the undo each time the next action after the duplicate. Counter cases: the redo of an undone delete works (run 3 row 35: Delete 7 -> 6, Cmd+Z 7, Cmd+Shift+Z 6; follow-up 8 by the toolbar and the Edit menu), the redo of an undone slide duplicate works (follow-up 5: Cmd+Y 2 -> 3 slides), and in follow-up 8 (deck untitled-20260916-6g42) a duplicate followed by a delete, two undos and Cmd+Shift+Z came back (5 -> 6), the Redo button reading enabled after that second undo. So the empty redo follows an undo issued straight after the duplicate; the follow-up 8 chain, where other steps came between, kept its redo.

rows.feature: Backspace or Delete with nothing selected on the canvas

rows.evidence: Follow-up 5 case 8 (deck untitled-20260916-zv03): empty sheet clicked (focus div.ts-stagewrap.ts-sheet, chip none), Backspace: slides 3 -> 2 and the next slide becomes current; Delete: slides 2 -> 1; after Edit > Delete had removed the last object (focus body), Backspace: slides 1 -> 0, the state reports no slide, the console logs a 400. Follow-up 4 section (e) hit the same: its Backspace after Edit > Delete removed the first slide and the probe stopped with "No slide title". In Google Slides the Delete key removes a slide only while the filmstrip has focus.

rows.interaction: With Snap to > Guides on, drag a rectangle so its left edge stops 4 px short of the guide at 600
rows.evidence: Follow-up 8 (deck untitled-20260916-6g42), Snap to > Guides on, a guide at x 600, the preview box read during the drag: pointer leaving A's left edge at 603 -> preview 600, landed 600; at 598 (a slow 40 step drag) -> preview 600, landed 600; at 596 -> preview 596, landed 596, with a different snap line drawn (an object line, not the guide's); at 597 from x 900 -> preview 596, landed 596, the same other line. Follow-up 7 (deck untitled-20260916-ez6v): at 596 -> landed 596 with one snap line drawn. The snap commits what it previews: an object edge snap (A's left edge left at 704 beside B's left edge 700) previewed 700 and landed 700, and the sheet centre snap (A's centre left at 796) previewed 800 and landed 800. So the guide takes the drag from 2 to 3 px away and loses it at 3 to 4 px when another line is drawn instead; a seller sees a snap line and lands 3 or 4 px off the guide.
rows.why: Snapping is how a seller lines things up without the Arrange menu.

rows.interaction: Hold Cmd while dragging to 4 px short of the guide
rows.evidence: Follow-up 7: the same drag to 596 with Cmd held drew no snap line (0, against 1 without Cmd) and landed at 596. The plain drag had landed at 596 as well (the guide snap row), so the override's effect shows in the missing snap line, not in the landing.
rows.why: A precision override.

rows.feature: Escape steps out of the text, then clears the selection
rows.interaction: Insert > Text box, click the slide, type a word, press Escape twice
rows.evidence: Run 3 (three tries, the same each time): Insert > Text box and a click on the sheet opened a text session (editing true), the word typed, Escape ended the session (editing false) and left the box selected (chip "Text box"), the second Escape cleared the selection (chip none). The script's own object lookup read the first slide while the stage showed another, so it reported the box as not found and marked the row failed; the behaviour it recorded is the expected one.
rows.why: Escape out of typing is constant work.
